LESSON: THE LORD’S PRAYER

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Church
Topic 5.4: The Lord’s Prayer

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Lord’s Prayer. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you pray always as a Christian?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. pray for parents, guardians and friends
2. say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE LORD’S PRAYER
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Lord’s Prayer helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE LORD’S PRAYER
Study The Lord’s Prayer like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Pray for parents, guardians and friends

What this means
In this part you learn to pray for parents, guardians and friends. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: pray for parents, guardians and friends.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Lord’s Prayer” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can pray for parents, guardians and friends. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually

What this means
In this part you learn to say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Lord’s Prayer in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Lord’s Prayer is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Lord’s Prayer” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: pray for parents, guardians and friends)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Lord’s Prayer in your own words. (skill: say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Lord’s Prayer to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: pray for parents, guardians and friends.
3. Practise this skill: say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually.
4. Make one local Kenya example of The Lord’s Prayer from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Lord’s Prayer: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study The Lord’s Prayer?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you pray always as a Christian?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Lord’s Prayer means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: pray for parents, guardians and friends.
5. Be able to: say a prayer to God every day to grow spiritually.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
